title: Why a project was deferred, and what funding it costs

blocks.text: The practice utility's planners (a fictional utility) read the best plan and ask about one project it left out: why is it deferred, and what would funding it cost? Milestone 4 answers both, for any project, with numbers a planner can check.

`why.py` gives you milestone 2's model and tools: `build(snapshot, scenario)` (a scenario's `force_in` list becomes a row $`\sum_t x_{i,t} \ge 1`$), `solve(b)` (HiGHS to a zero gap), `plan_of(b, result)` and `check(snapshot, scenario, plan)`, the rule checker that names every row a plan breaks from the data alone.

items: `refused_by(snapshot, scenario, plan, pid)`: for each start year $`t`$ of the deferred project, the rows that **the plan as it stands, with the project added at $`t`$**, breaks (lesson 9.3.1: on a MILP the row that blocks is the one a whole project cannot fit, slack or not). Return `{start year: [row names]}`, with each list exactly as `check` returns it: `must_` rows, then `alt_`, then `after_`, then for each year in order its `budget_`, `region_` and `crews_` rows, then `floor_` rows. Rows the plan already breaks without the project are not taken out: they are listed at every start.

`forcing_cost(snapshot, scenario, pid)`: solve the scenario, then solve it again with `pid` forced in (lesson 9.3.2). Return `Forced(cost, gives_way)`, where `cost` is the base objective less the forced one, and `gives_way` lists, by project id, every project of the base plan that the forced plan drops (`"J3 dropped"`) or moves (`"J1 2028->2027"`). When the forced model has no plan, return `None`: a forcing the rules cannot satisfy is answered by a rule, not by a price.

`cost_interval(base_primal, base_bound, forced_primal, forced_bound)`: on a large portfolio both solves stop at a relative gap, so each objective is only known between its plan's value (primal) and its proven bound. For a maximization, the true cost lies between
Return the pair `(low, high)`. Forcing a project in can never raise the best value, which is why the low end is never below zero.

cases.says: forcing the deferred project in costs the NPV the best plan loses, and a project that gives way is named
each start is refused by the rows the plan as it stands would break with the project added, not by the project alone
what gives way lists the projects that move to another year as well as those dropped
a forcing that no plan allows is answered with no price at all
when both solves stop at a gap, the cost lies between the base plan less the forced bound and the base bound less the forced plan
forcing a project in never gains NPV, so the low end of the interval is never below zero
a row the plan already breaks without the project is still listed at every start

concepts: the rows that refuse a deferred project as the plan stands, and the price of forcing it in, as a number or an interval
